narrative: The web-frontend pipeline on build-runner-09 installed a typosquatted dependency, colour-picker@3.1.9, whose postinstall hook ran a remote shell (ci_build.jsonl:5) and read the CI pipeline secrets NPM_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and GH_PAT (ci_build.jsonl:6). The build host — which should only receive inbound traffic — then beaconed outbound to a malicious endpoint at 203.0.113.91 four times (fw_traffic.jsonl:2-5), and a published artifact carried an unexpected extra bundle chunk (app_payments.jsonl:1). Blast radius: build-runner-09, the colour-picker dependency, and the three stolen CI secrets.
decoy: A legitimate major version bump of webpack to 5.92.0 broke 12 unit tests (ci_build.jsonl:3-4), which looks like a malicious dependency change. But webpack 5.92.0 is an official release rated benign in threat_intel.csv:3, it ran no install-time scripts, and it caused no outbound traffic — a failing test is not a compromise. A correct agent must NOT attribute the supply-chain attack to webpack and must self-correct to colour-picker.
root_cause: A typosquatted npm dependency executed a postinstall hook that stole CI secrets and exfiltrated them from the build host, which then beaconed for command-and-control.
